finding.claim: /checkout computes the charge total from client-supplied price and qty. An attacker can set price to 0.01 or negative, or qty to negative, and pay arbitrarily little (or a negative total, which may credit or refund the account).

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty taken directly from the request body, with no catalog lookup, no bounds check and no integer check
total is passed straight to the payment charge
the attacker-chosen total is returned as the amount charged

finding.guards_checked: No catalog price lookup, no validation that qty is a positive integer, no check that price is non-negative, and no check that total > 0. The safer /checkout-v2 route does a server-side price lookup and clamps qty, which shows the intended control is missing here. Auth or validation middleware is not in this file; nothing in cart.js constrains the values.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price*i.qty with no validation and cart.js:6 passes it to req.payments.charge, while /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14) shows the missing catalog lookup and qty clamp; no other middleware or files exist in the directory, and any logged-in user (req.user) can reach it.
